Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12

Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (VesperMedia VP Eng), Samir Patel (VesperMedia SRE Lead), Li Chen (CTO), Ana Torres (Product)

Summary: Post-incident review focused on long-tail throttling that caused latency tail spikes across several inference routes. Discussed rollback vs mitigations, telemetry blindspots, and an immediate canary plan.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Nguyen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know we squeezed this in quick after the spike this morning, um so goal is to align on rollback vs targeted mitigations and get sprint work assigned.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: yeah thanks alex, we are — still feeling the customer pressure, multiple third‑party vendors pinging, um our ops pager hit repeatedly. want to make sure we can either revert or patch quickly.
[00:35] Priya Kapoor: quick note, we've seen the same pattern in our internal traces — long tail requests that hit fallback model variants and then amplify latency. looks like a prefix cache miss pattern in a subset of routes.
[00:52] Samir Patel: to add, the traffic spikes aligned with a small config push last wednesday, but not 100% correlated. some of the routes have aggressive batching enabled, others are single token low‑latency requests.
[01:10] Li Chen: can you clarify fallback amplification? is that an autoscale issue or model variant selection problem?
[01:22] Priya Kapoor: good question — fallback amplification here means when the primary execution path fails fast (OOM or timeouts), requests are routed to a heavier model variant that has longer cold start and larger KV cache pressure, so overall tail latency increases. it's not autoscale in the classical sense, it's more about routing to compat variants.
[01:45] Marta Ruiz: ok so the immediate ask from our side is either a fast rollback to the prior model/deploy or a surgical config change to routing rules. what's the risk to data or compliance for rollback?
[02:01] Alex Nguyen: rollback is operationally straightforward from Redwood side — but we do need your approval matrix for rollbacks that affect production routes, and we should check if any customer-specified retention or audit windows would be impacted. we flagged the SOC2 and KMS notes in the shared doc.
[02:20] Ana Torres: just to be clear product wise — rolling back may change embedding outputs for downstream ranking, which will affect user facing features, we need to measure quality impact.
[02:37] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll capture quality delta with the eval harness during a canary. recommended approach: 2% traffic to rollback canary, capture latency histograms, and run evals against key prompts.
[02:58] Samir Patel: samir here — we can route 2% with our traffic splitter, but we need Redwood to confirm the exact deploy id to pin. also will need trace IDs for any elevated errors.
[03:15] Alex Nguyen: noted. priya — can you take the lead on a staging canary and capture token-level latency histograms?
[03:25] Priya Kapoor: yep i'll schedule the canary on staging first, then run in prod if staging looks good. will enable verbose traces for KV cache hits.
[03:36] Marta Ruiz: what about telemetry gaps — we had trouble correlating requests with backend KVs because of sampling. can we get full traces for 48 hours?
[03:49] Priya Kapoor: we can increase sampling on our side but also need your side to emit the route/deploy metadata in headers, otherwise traces are hard to stitch.
[04:05] Li Chen: we can add headers but there's potential perf cost — how granular do you need them?
[04:12] Priya Kapoor: ideally deploy id, route id, and a short request hash. that should be low overhead.
[04:22] Alex Nguyen: quick aside — we noticed in logs that KV cache hit metric reporting sometimes lags by several minutes under heavy pressure, which hides the onset of cascade. that's something we'll surface to the runtime team.
[04:37] Marta Ruiz: ok. going back to rollback gating — what are our options operationally? full rollback, canary, or routing rule change to avoid variant selection?
[04:50] Priya Kapoor: routing change is lower-impact if you can accept slightly different model variant for a small subset. full rollback flips all routes back which is faster to implement but riskier for product quality. canary is a middle ground.
[05:07] Samir Patel: how long would a full rollback take?
[05:11] Alex Nguyen: from Redwood side, a rollback on a model/service tag is minutes, but the time to validate and approve is the long pole. also we need to consider cache warmup and tokenization differences.
[05:27] Li Chen: cache warmup concerns are big — if we rollback we might cold start a lot of KV entries and see a temporary spike, right?
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: yep, there's often a brief hit while the KV prefix cache refills. we can mitigate with pre-warming scripts for common prefixes, but that's best effort.
[05:48] Marta Ruiz: can pre-warm be scheduled as part of rollback?
[05:52] Priya Kapoor: yes, but it requires a sample of top prefix keys from your traffic to be effective.
[06:01] Alex Nguyen: let's capture top 500 prefixes from the affected routes. samir can share those logs.
[06:06] Samir Patel: will do. i'll put a link to the extracted prefixes in the ticket.
[06:11] Ana Torres: any security approvals needed if we snapshot logs for pre-warm?
[06:17] Alex Nguyen: we should redact PII and follow your retention rules — we'll coordinate with your security. also will include KMS key usage notes.
[06:27] Li Chen: one more question about the fallback model — is it a newer or older variant?
[06:33] Priya Kapoor: in this case fallback is an older, beefier variant we keep for compatibility. it has larger memory footprint and slower latency, so when routed to it under load latency spikes.
[06:45] Marta Ruiz: ok would toggling routing threshold help? like only route to fallback on 500ms threshold instead of 200ms?
[06:55] Priya Kapoor: possibly, but that could increase error surface if primary fails silently. we need to carefully tune.
[07:04] Alex Nguyen: timeline proposal: immediate canary in 24 hours, collect metrics for 12 hours, make rollback decision at 48 hours. does that work?
[07:15] Marta Ruiz: yes that's acceptable as long as we get clear pass/fail criteria.
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: pass criteria: 99th percentile latency returns to baseline within 10% and error rate does not increase. also quality eval within acceptable threshold.
[07:34] Samir Patel: fail criteria: tail latency stays above 2x baseline or error rate doubles.
[07:42] Alex Nguyen: good. i'll own coordination with your ops to schedule the canary.
[07:49] Marta Ruiz: alex can you also share a runbook snippet for rollback steps, we want to keep it lightweight.
[07:55] Alex Nguyen: yes i'll put a 1‑pager in the shared drive with exact commands and rollback gating.
[08:03] Priya Kapoor: quick technical note — we saw intermittent 503s that aligned with a particular GPU pool, might be a hardware-preemption pattern, worth checking Dedicated vs Hosted if you have mixed traffic.
[08:18] Li Chen: we run mixed. 40% on Redwood hosted, 60% on dedicated in us‑east. could that cause routing mismatches?
[08:27] Priya Kapoor: potentially — routing policies can pick different model artifacts or quantized builds per pool. we should ensure artifact equivalence across pools and that autoscale configs are aligned.
[08:40] Marta Ruiz: do you have a tool to validate artifact parity?
[08:44] Alex Nguyen: we have a parity-check script that compares model checksums and config flags across deploys. priya will run that.
[08:52] Priya Kapoor: i'll run parity checks and report mismatches.
[08:57] Ana Torres: curious about auditing requirements — if we rollback, will audit logs show the change and who initiated?
[09:04] Alex Nguyen: yes, Redwood audit logs track model tag changes, who initiated, and key rotation events. we'll export an audit slice for your compliance team.
[09:13] Samir Patel: perfect. also can we get a snippet of the KMS rotation policy?
[09:18] Alex Nguyen: sure, will share KMS policy excerpt.
[09:22] Marta Ruiz: ok next — sprint assignments. who will do what?
[09:27] Alex Nguyen: propose: redwood owns canary and parity checks; customer owns prefixes extract and rollback approval matrix; joint ownership for telemetry instrumentation.
[09:36] Samir Patel: makes sense. i'll own prefix extraction and headers emission.
[09:40] Li Chen: i'll sign off on any rollback for full prod after sprint review.
[09:46] Priya Kapoor: i'll schedule the canary run and capture histograms + quality evals.
[09:52] Alex Nguyen: noted. action items in the doc.
[09:56] Marta Ruiz: anything else on security?
[10:00] Alex Nguyen: we'll include SOC2 audit snippet and note that data in traces will be redacted, and provide instructions for KMS key rotation visibility.
[10:10] Ana Torres: okay great.
[10:13] Alex Nguyen: final recap: redwood will run parity checks, run staging canary, and prepare rollback 1‑pager; customer will provide prefixes, deploy ids, and approval matrix. follow‑up meeting Wednesday 2026-11-14 at 15:00 UTC to decide on full rollback.
[10:33] Marta Ruiz: thanks everyone.
[10:36] Li Chen: thanks.
[10:38] Samir Patel: thanks bye.

End of transcript.
